title: Attorney General of South Dakota

context.text: Attorney General Marty Jackley is not seeking re-election; he won the Republican nomination for the U.S. House in the June 2, 2026 primary. South Dakota parties choose their attorney general nominees at conventions: Lance Russell won the Republican nomination on June 27, 2026, receiving 57% in the second round of voting over Austin Hoffman (31%) and John Fitzgerald (12%).
Democrats did not field a candidate and there are no third-party or independent candidates, so Russell is unopposed on the November ballot.

candidates.name: Lance Russell
candidates.ballotNote: Nominated at the June 27, 2026 Republican state convention; unopposed in the general election.
candidates.currentRole: State's Attorney of Fall River and Oglala Lakota counties

summary.text: Lance Russell is the Republican nominee and the only candidate for attorney general on the ballot. He is the state's attorney for Fall River and Oglala Lakota counties and lives in Hot Springs. He won the nomination in a three-way, two-round convention vote.

background.text: State's attorney of Fall River and Oglala Lakota counties.

sources.title: State's top election official loses nomination to challenger who supports hand-counting

researchNotes: Slate: confirmed on the South Dakota Secretary of State's official 2026 General Election Candidate List (Lance Russell, REP, the only Attorney General entry) and by South Dakota Searchlight. No campaign website, questionnaire or public policy statements for Russell were found (several likely domains were tried; Ballotpedia has no profile), so no priorities or positions are listed and his state's attorney casework was not researched.
